sources.description: The 111 m Saturn V accelerated the Apollo spacecraft to orbital velocity, roughly 28,000 km/h (about 7.8 km/s).
Halley's Comet has a nucleus about 15 km long; at perihelion it races past the Sun at around 254,000 km/h (70.56 km/s).
A Formula One car stands only about 0.95 m tall and reaches top speeds near 375 km/h (233 mph).
A Suzuki Hayabusa is about 1.16 m tall and tops out around 300 km/h (early models hit 312 km/h before speed-limiting agreements).
Ken Warby's Spirit of Australia, a jet-powered hydroplane, set the world water speed record of 511 km/h (318 mph) in 1978 — still unbeaten.
The men's speed-skiing world record is 255.5 km/h, set by Simon Billy in Vars, France in 2023.
The Mexican free-tailed bat, about 9 cm long, has been radar-tracked in level flight at up to 160 km/h — the fastest horizontal flight of any animal.
A homing pigeon averages about 97 km/h over long distances; top racers have been clocked up to 160 km/h with a tailwind.
A competition luge slider reaches about 140 km/h (the track record is ~154 km/h) lying on a small sled.
A three-toed sloth is about 45 cm long and tops out around 0.27 km/h (4.6 m/min, in the trees) — the slowest land mammal.
A common bottlenose dolphin is about 3 m long and can burst up to about 35 km/h.
A large male saltwater crocodile reaches about 6 m in length and can swim in short bursts of about 24-29 km/h.
A large great white shark is about 5 m long (range 3.5-6 m) and can reach burst speeds approaching 50 km/h.
A declassified 1950 FBI memo described flying saucers (per Roswell-era reports) as circular and about 50 ft (15.24 m) in diameter.
Kenneth Arnold, whose 1947 sighting coined the term 'flying saucer', estimated the objects' speed at no less than 1,200 mph (~1,930 km/h).
An N700 series Shinkansen (Japanese bullet train) car is about 3.63 m tall and runs at a maximum operating speed of 300 km/h (on the San'yō line).
Tall tornado funnels can reach roughly 1,500 m, from ground to cloud base; no official height record exists.
The highest tornado wind speed ever measured was about 517 km/h (321 mph, after 2021 reanalysis) in the 1999 Bridge Creek-Moore tornado.
The Lovell Telescope at Jodrell Bank, a steerable dish radio telescope, stands about 89 m tall (76 m dish).
The Rajagopuram of Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam, is the tallest gopuram at 73 m.
A traditional African rondavel (round thatched hut) stands roughly 4 m tall (walls plus a conical roof rising 2-4 m).
A Bell 206 JetRanger, a common light helicopter, is 2.85 m tall on its skids and has a maximum speed of about 226 km/h (122 kn).
A regulation curling stone has a minimum height of 11.4 cm (4.5 in).
An American cockroach is about 4 cm long and can run at 5.4 km/h — roughly 50 body lengths per second.
A bald eagle stands roughly 61 cm tall (body length 70-102 cm, wingspan up to ~2.3 m); it glides at 56-70 km/h and can dive at 120-160 km/h.
A mountain troll in the Harry Potter universe stands twelve feet (about 366 cm) tall, the largest breed of troll.
A regulation size 7 basketball is about 24 cm in diameter (circumference ~75 cm).
A regulation size 5 football is about 22 cm in diameter (circumference 68-70 cm).
A regulation tennis ball is 6.54-6.86 cm in diameter (about 6.7 cm).
A regulation baseball is about 7.4 cm in diameter (circumference 22.9-23.5 cm).
A Galápagos giant tortoise stands roughly 80 cm tall overall (recorded shell lengths reach ~1.3-1.5 m) and ambles at about 0.3 km/h.
Apple's official tech specs list the AirPods Max height as 187.3 mm (18.7 cm), including cushions.
A typical stiletto heel is about 9-10 cm tall; the shoe as it stands reaches roughly 12 cm at the top of the heel counter.
A standard taco uses a ~15 cm tortilla; folded and filled it stands roughly 8 cm tall.
Falcon's Flight at Six Flags Qiddiya City stands 163 m tall and reaches 250 km/h.
A piece of nigiri sushi sits about 3 cm tall (rice base ~1.5-2 cm plus the fish topping).
A mosquito is a weak flyer, managing only about 1-1.5 km/h.
Wood ants preferred about 11 cm/s (0.396 km/h) in a level-walking study; this is not their maximum speed.
A housefly cruises at about 7 km/h (4.5 mph), with brief bursts up to ~24 km/h.
Radar tracking has found ladybirds flying at up to 60 km/h (averaging ~30 km/h), often at altitudes of 150-500 m.
A honeybee flies at about 24 km/h (15 mph), slower when laden with nectar or pollen.
A garden snail (Cornu aspersum) has a recorded maximum speed of about 0.047 km/h (roughly 1.3 cm/s).
A house mouse can run at up to about 13 km/h (8 mph).
A Fujifilm X100VI compact camera is 74.8 mm (7.5 cm) tall.
The average adult human heart is about 12 cm in length (roughly the size of a fist).
A domestic cat can sprint at up to about 48 km/h (30 mph) over short distances.
Pufferfish are slow swimmers, propelling themselves with their fins at up to about 3 body lengths per second — roughly 3 km/h for a 30 cm fish.
A domestic rooster stands roughly 35 cm tall and can run at about 14 km/h (≈9 mph), with faster birds reaching well above that.
A European rabbit can run at up to about 56 km/h (35 mph) to escape predators.
A mallard cruises at 40-60 km/h and can reach about 90 km/h in fast flight.
A fit standard poodle, bred as an athletic water retriever, can run at roughly 45 km/h.
A great horned owl can fly at more than 65 km/h (40 mph) in level flight.
A rhesus macaque can run at up to about 32 km/h (20 mph).
An average healthy dog runs at about 24-32 km/h; the fastest breeds, like greyhounds, reach ~72 km/h.
A goat can run at roughly 24 km/h (15 mph).
A domestic pig can run at up to about 19 km/h (12 mph) in short sprints.
A North American river otter can swim at up to about 13 km/h (8 mph).
A leopard can sprint at up to about 58 km/h (36 mph) in short bursts.
A flamingo flies at about 50-60 km/h on migration.
A tiger can reach roughly 49-65 km/h in a short charge.
A white-tailed deer can sprint at up to about 60 km/h (37 mph).
An Indian peafowl runs at about 16 km/h and can manage short bursts of flight around 30 km/h.
A hippopotamus can run at about 30 km/h (19 mph) on land over short distances.
Orangutans are built for the trees; on the ground they amble at only about 1.6 km/h (1 mph).
A cow can run at up to about 40 km/h (25 mph) in short bursts.
A red kangaroo cruises at 20-25 km/h, sustains 40 km/h, and can hop at up to about 70 km/h over short distances.
A galloping horse averages 40-48 km/h; a racing Thoroughbred has been clocked around 70 km/h over a sprint.
A typical recreational runner jogs at about 8-10 km/h; elite sprinters peak near 45 km/h, but that's far from a normal running pace.
A llama can run at up to about 56 km/h (35 mph).
A gorilla can sprint at up to about 40 km/h (25 mph) during a charge.
A camel can reach about 65 km/h (40 mph) in short sprints and sustain ~40 km/h for an hour.
Taking a classic VW Beetle as a representative car, the top speed is about 130 km/h (≈82 mph for the 1300/1500 models).
A white rhinoceros can charge at about 50 km/h (31 mph) over short distances.
An American bison can run at up to about 56 km/h (35 mph) despite weighing close to a tonne.
Analyses of the 1967 Patterson-Gimlin film estimate the figure was walking at about 9 km/h (5.7 mph).
A standard urban fire engine (pumper) reaches a top speed of roughly 100 km/h (≈60-65 mph); most are governed around that figure.
An African bush elephant can move at up to about 40 km/h (25 mph) in a short charge.
A large male woolly mammoth stood about 3.35 m tall; its estimated top speed is roughly 40 km/h, like an elephant.
Urban transit monorails reach top speeds around 80 km/h (e.g. Bologna's Marconi Express); theme-park and airport shuttles run slower.
The LNER Mallard set the steam locomotive speed record of 203 km/h (126 mph) in 1938.
The 1970 Huascarán debris avalanche reached speeds of up to about 435 km/h (270 mph), one of the fastest mass movements recorded.
A modern road-going farm tractor tops out around 50 km/h (≈31 mph); field work is done far slower.
A giraffe can gallop at up to about 60 km/h over short distances (cruising nearer 16 km/h).
Biomechanical studies estimate Tyrannosaurus rex topped out at roughly 20-30 km/h — a fast walk rather than a true run.
An orca can reach burst speeds of about 55 km/h (34 mph) when hunting, making it one of the fastest marine mammals.
Taking a Cessna 172 as a representative small airplane, it cruises at about 226 km/h (122 kn).
A trolleybus usually tops out around 60-65 km/h, with some designs reaching 80 km/h.
A conventional bus is typically governed to around 100 km/h on motorways (lower with standing passengers).
A tram runs at 30-50 km/h in street traffic but can reach about 80 km/h on segregated track.
Fossil trackways indicate sauropods generally ambled at about 3-5 km/h, rarely exceeding ~7 km/h.
Fictional: analysis of Game of Thrones flight times suggests the dragons cruised around 140 mph (~226 km/h), about as fast as a small airliner.
A blue whale cruises at 3-6 km/h but can burst to around 35 km/h when threatened.
A Boeing 747 jetliner cruises at about Mach 0.85, roughly 900 km/h (490 kn).
The International Space Station orbits Earth at about 27,600 km/h (7.66 km/s).
Las Vegas's High Roller stands 167.6 m tall.
The Moon orbits Earth at about 3,683 km/h (1.022 km/s).
Earth orbits the Sun at an average speed of about 107,200 km/h (29.78 km/s).
Saturn orbits the Sun at an average speed of about 34,800 km/h (9.68 km/s).
The Sun orbits the center of the Milky Way at about 828,000 km/h (~230 km/s).
Lightning's return stroke travels at about 321,868,800 km/h; its initial leader is slower. This is not light speed.
Light in vacuum travels at exactly 299,792,458 m/s (the constant c). The universe’s speed limit.
The Milky Way moves at about 1,987,000 km/h (552 km/s) relative to the cosmic microwave background.
A study of 18 earthworms found an average surface crawling speed of about 30 cm/min (0.018 km/h).
A moon jelly can reach about 40 cm across its bell; diameter is used as its representative size.
Caltech reports typical jellyfish swimming at about 2 cm/s (0.072 km/h), excluding drifting or stimulation.
Adult Grammostola tarantulas are roughly 6 cm in body length; body length is used rather than leg span.
Male G. vachoni tarantulas averaged 4.12 cm/s (0.14832 km/h) in sprints at 10°C; warmer conditions affect speed.
Representative fair-weather cumulus cloud about 1 km from base to top; real cloud depth varies greatly.
Geneva's Jet d'Eau sends its water jet to an altitude of about 150 m.
The Stena Hollandica is 240.87 m long and has a maximum speed of 22 knots (about 40.7 km/h).
IMOCA 60 racing yachts have a hull length of 60 ft (18.29 m).
Malizia-Seaexplorer averaged about 35.4 knots (65.5 km/h) during its record 24-hour IMOCA run.
Sebastian Steudtner's record Nazaré wave was measured at 26.21 m high. Wave speed is omitted because it depends on depth and wavelength.
A representative medium pizza is 12 in (about 30.5 cm) in diameter.
A Cirque du Soleil Grand Chapiteau big top stands about 19 m high.
World Pool-Billiard Association pool balls are 2.25 in (57.15 mm) in diameter.
A brown rat reaches about 28 cm in head-and-body length and can run at roughly 11 km/h.
Adult male water buffalo typically stand 129–133 cm at the withers.
Water buffalo can run at about 48 km/h (30 mph).
A mature forest tent caterpillar is about 5–5.5 cm long.
Atlantic bluefin tuna can reach about 4.6 m in length and swim at roughly 70 km/h (43 mph).
An eastern gray squirrel's body is about 23–30 cm long and it can sprint near 32 km/h.
The familiar 3.5-inch floppy disk cartridge is about 94 mm tall.
A standard compact disc is 120 mm in diameter.
A representative Hass avocado is about 12 cm long; individual fruit size varies.
A large adult European hedgehog reaches about 26 cm in head-and-body length.
European hedgehogs can run at about 9.7 km/h (6 mph).
An adult two-spotted field cricket is about 2–2.5 cm long.
A representative mature garlic bulb is about 6 cm across.
A large Canada goose reaches about 110 cm in length and commonly flies around 65 km/h.
A representative table olive is about 3 cm long; cultivar sizes vary.
The Wuppertal suspension railway is a 13.3 km system whose trains reach 60 km/h.
Whistler's Peak 2 Peak Gondola spans 4.4 km and runs at 7.5 m/s (27 km/h).
Ever Given is 399.94 m long and has a service speed of 22.8 knots (about 42.2 km/h).
Icon of the Seas is 364.75 m long and has a maximum speed of 22 knots (about 40.7 km/h).
International sprint C-1 canoes have a maximum length of 5.2 m.
Elite 200 m sprint-canoe performances around 38.3 seconds average roughly 18.8 km/h.
